answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. New agents must stake collateral on a basalt bedrock registry, where each duplicate node in a local cluster triggers an exponential capital exhaustion spiral: the staking cost scales superlinearly as $O(k^2)$. Across this decentralized meadow of peers, swarms face prohibitive resource depletion while honest agents verify proofs cheaply.
